f.title: Comply with the obligations in Schedule 1 (CSA Model Code principles)
f.statement: Subject to sections 6 to 9, every organization must comply with the obligations set out in Schedule 1 (the principles of the CSA Model Code, clauses 4.1 to 4.10).
f.applicability: Organizations subject to PIPEDA Part 1 in respect of personal information they collect, use or disclose in the course of commercial activities (s. 4(1)); Part 1 does not apply to government institutions to which the Privacy Act applies (s. 4(2)(a)). f.exceptions: Subject to sections 6 to 9 (consent, access and related exceptions). "Should" in Schedule 1 is a recommendation only (s. 5(2)).

f.statement: Under s. 7(3)(c.1), an organization may disclose personal information without the knowledge or consent of the individual to a government institution or part of a government institution that has made a request for the information, identified its lawful authority to obtain the information and indicated that (among the listed grounds) the disclosure is requested for the purpose of administering any law of Canada or a province (subparagraph (iii)); the other grounds are national security, defence or international affairs (i), law enforcement (ii) and communicating with next of kin of an injured, ill or deceased individual (iv).

f.applicability: Organizations subject to PIPEDA Part 1 in respect of personal information they collect, use or disclose in the course of commercial activities (s. 4(1)); Part 1 does not apply to government institutions to which the Privacy Act applies (s. 4(2)(a)). f.title: Prospective business transaction: use and disclose without consent only under a protective agreement
f.statement: Organizations that are parties to a prospective business transaction may use and disclose personal information without the knowledge or consent of the individual if (a) they have entered into an agreement that requires the receiving organization to use and disclose that information solely for purposes related to the transaction, to protect it by security safeguards appropriate to its sensitivity, and, if the transaction does not proceed, to return or destroy it within a reasonable time; and (b) the information is necessary to determine whether to proceed with the transaction and, if the determination is made to proceed, to complete it.
f.applicability: Organizations subject to PIPEDA Part 1 in respect of personal information they collect, use or disclose in the course of commercial activities (s. 4(1)); Part 1 does not apply to government institutions to which the Privacy Act applies (s. 4(2)(a)). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects. Curator note (not in the text): relevant to safety database transfers in product divestments and acquisitions.
f.exceptions: Does not apply to a transaction whose primary purpose or result is the purchase, sale or other acquisition or disposition, or lease, of personal information (s. 7.2(4)).

f.title: Amend inaccurate or incomplete information and, where appropriate, transmit the amendment to third parties
f.statement: When an individual successfully demonstrates the inaccuracy or incompleteness of personal information, the organization must amend the information as required. Depending upon the nature of the information challenged, amendment involves the correction, deletion, or addition of information. Where appropriate, the amended information must be transmitted to third parties having access to the information in question.
f.applicability: Organizations subject to PIPEDA Part 1 in respect of personal information they collect, use or disclose in the course of commercial activities (s. 4(1)); Part 1 does not apply to government institutions to which the Privacy Act applies (s. 4(2)(a)). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects. Curator note (not in the text): in PV this may mean a follow-up report to recipients of the case.
